newsitem.title: USA: GM's Buick to discontinue Skylark.
newsitem.headline: GM's Buick to discontinue Skylark.

text.p: General Motors Corp said production of Buick's compact Skylark will conclude with the 1998 model.

For the 1998 model year, the coupe will be dropped and Skylark will be produced only as a four-door sedan that will be exclusively sold to fleet buyers, said Joseph Fitzsimmons, Buick's brand manager for Skylark and LeSabre.
Despite recent brisk sales for Skylark, Buick's long-term strategy is to move Buick entry level customers toward the Century and Regal brands, it said.
The Skylark name has appeared several times in the Buick lineup. The first time was in 1953, when a limited-edition convertible was offered as a Buick 50th anniversary model.

The Skylark name appeared in 1962 on a small convertible and coupe and remained in the lineup through the 1972 model year. The name was revived on a 1975 compact car and has been part of the lineup, as a compact, ever since.
